slides.title: Real apps are lists you can change.
slides.html:
The big idea

Real apps are lists you can change.

Tasks, jobs, students, orders: most apps show a list, let you add to it, edit it and delete from it. This week you build exactly that.

Full-Stack Development · Week 4 · React in Practice

slides.title: Controlled forms
slides.html:
Forms

Controlled forms

  • Keep each input's value in state
  • One object in state for the whole form
  • [e.target.name] updates the right field
  • preventDefault stops the page reloading

JobForm.jsx

const [form, setForm] = useState({ title: "", company: "" });
 
const handleChange = (e) =>
  setForm({ ...form, [e.target.name]: e.target.value });
 
const handleSubmit = (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  if (!form.title) return alert("Add a title");
  onAdd(form);
  setForm({ title: "", company: "" });
};
 
<input name="title" value={form.title}
  onChange={handleChange} />

slides.title: Add, edit and delete
slides.html:
Lists

Add, edit and delete

  • Never change the array in state directly
  • Add: spread it into a new array
  • Delete: filter it out
  • Edit: map and replace the one that matches

App.jsx

const [tasks, setTasks] = useState([]);
 
const addTask = (text) =>
  setTasks([...tasks, { id: Date.now(), text, done: false }]);
 
const deleteTask = (id) =>
  setTasks(tasks.filter((t) => t.id !== id));
 
const toggleTask = (id) =>
  setTasks(tasks.map((t) =>
    t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t
  ));

slides.title: Side effects with useEffect
slides.html:
Hooks

Side effects with useEffect

  • Effects run after React draws the screen
  • Use them for fetching, timers, localStorage
  • The dependency array controls when it runs
  • [] means once, when the component appears

App.jsx

useEffect(() => {
  document.title = `${tasks.length} tasks`;
}, [tasks]);          // runs when tasks changes
 
useEffect(() => {
  const saved = localStorage.getItem("tasks");
  if (saved) setTasks(JSON.parse(saved));
}, []);               // runs once
 
useEffect(() => {
  localStorage.setItem("tasks", JSON.stringify(tasks));
}, [tasks]);

slides.title: Reusable components
slides.html:
Components

Reusable components

  • Make components that work with any data
  • Use props for text, colours and actions
  • children lets you put anything inside
  • Write once, use everywhere

Button.jsx

function Button({ children, variant = "primary", ...rest }) {
  return (
    <button className={`btn btn-${variant}`} {...rest}>
      {children}
    </button>
  );
}
 
<Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="danger" onClick={remove}>
  Delete
</Button>

slides.title: Organising files and folders
slides.html:
Structure

Organising files and folders

  • components/: small reusable pieces
  • pages/: one file per page
  • hooks/, services/: shared logic and API calls
  • One component per file, named the same

Project structure

src/
  components/
    Button.jsx
    JobCard.jsx
    Navbar.jsx
  pages/
    Home.jsx
    JobDetails.jsx
    NotFound.jsx
  services/
    api.js
  App.jsx
  main.jsx

slides.title: Pages with React Router
slides.html:
Routing

Pages with React Router

  • One app, many pages, no full reloads
  • Routes maps URLs to page components
  • Link instead of <a> for inside links
  • :id in a path is a URL parameter

main.jsx

npm install react-router-dom
 
<BrowserRouter>
  <Navbar />
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="/jobs/:id" element={<JobDetails />} />
    <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />
  </Routes>
</BrowserRouter>
 
<Link to={`/jobs/${job.id}`}>View job</Link>
const { id } = useParams();

slides.title: Your app can show data from anywhere on the internet.
slides.html:
APIs

Your app can show data from anywhere on the internet.

An API is a web address that sends back data, usually as JSON. You fetch it, then put it in state.

slides.title: Fetching data from an API
slides.html:
APIs

Fetching data from an API

  • Fetch inside useEffect
  • Track loading and error in state
  • Always show something while you wait

Users.jsx

const [users, setUsers] = useState([]);
const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
const [error, setError] = useState("");
 
useEffect(() => {
  fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users")
    .then((res) => res.json())
    .then((data) => setUsers(data))
    .catch(() => setError("Could not load users"))
    .finally(() => setLoading(false));
}, []);
 
if (loading) return <p>Loading…</p>;
if (error) return <p>{error}</p>;

Styling

Ways to style React apps

Plain CSS

Import a .css file into a component. Simple and familiar.

import "./App.css";

CSS Modules

Class names scoped to one component, so they never clash.

Tailwind CSS

Utility classes right in your JSX. Very popular and fast.

slides.title: Saving and showing the list
slides.html:
Build

Saving and showing the list

  • State holds the list
  • useEffect saves it to localStorage
  • Each item is a reusable card

App.jsx

export default function App() {
  const [jobs, setJobs] = useState([]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    localStorage.setItem("jobs", JSON.stringify(jobs));
  }, [jobs]);
 
  const addJob = (job) => setJobs([{ ...job, id: Date.now() }, ...jobs]);
  const removeJob = (id) => setJobs(jobs.filter((j) => j.id !== id));
 
  return jobs.map((j) => (
    <JobCard key={j.id} job={j} onRemove={removeJob} />
  ));
}
